correctness.rationale: The centered-Gaussian scores are exactly the exposed-vertex support values, with endpoint variance 2, bulk variance 6, covariance lags -2/3 and 1/6, and endpoint covariance at sites 2,3 equal to -3,+1. Blocking with two-site gaps proves a Gumbel maximum for the 2-dependent bulk. Mills ratio yields the endpoint density coefficient 4 sqrt(3) pi exp(-3y) on the n^3/log(n) scale; the integral against exp(-exp(-y)) is Gamma(3)=2. Independent-subsequence survival bounds dominate the left tail and elementary Gaussian bounds suppress omitted local scores, giving 8 sqrt(3) pi. The analogous variance-6 integral yields uniform interior angle 1/n, and the star hub event tends to a normal halfspace. Actual path score-covariance, sampling and importance-sampling code was executed and succeeded. Computations are finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: A normal-cone angle is the intrinsic probability that random linear optimization exposes a given vertex, so its all-order asymptotic is a central geometric functional of a natural graph polytope. The sharp cubic log-corrected suppression of two endpoint orbits compared with order 1/n at their immediate neighbors is a nontrivial and qualitatively surprising boundary phenomenon. The star’s hub mass 1/2 demonstrates that uniform lattice equivalence does not control random Euclidean exposure, a motivated structural obstruction that goes beyond a routine Gaussian moment calculation.
